title: Reimagine slim field annotations and collision resolution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dense and compact form surfaces currently exhibit unpredictable collisions between inline annotations (errors, hints, suggestions) and adjacent controls when screen width or density changes. This causes clipped copy, overlapping microcopy and inconsistent keyboard focus targets, which complicates developer adoption and increases support tickets for complex forms (multi-column, inline-edit).

Goal: Define a single, implementable protocol for "slim" field annotations that: (1) prioritizes validation messages vs. ephemeral hints; (2) stabilizes layout across density tokens and responsive breakpoints; (3) specifies accessible focus and screen-reader behavior; and (4) provides a small set of tokens and CSS hooks for engineers to adopt without heavy per-component overrides. Deliverables include token recommendations, a Figma component kit, acceptance criteria, and a short handoff checklist for engineering and QA.
acceptance_criteria: A centralized token mapping (compact/regular/comfortable) that defines spacing, min-height, line-clamp rules and z-index for annotations is published and approved by design and frontend leads
Inline validation messages have deterministic priority ordering (error > warning > success > hint) and a defined animation/no-animation option for low-power contexts
When two annotation types would overlap in narrow widths, the protocol defines which to hide/collapse and how to expose hidden info (aria-live, inline disclosure)
A Figma kit with three responsive field variants and example states (empty, typing, suggestion list open, error, warning, collapsed hint) is added to the system library
Engineering implements a small CSS utility set (+ JS fallback) documented in the handoff and passes accessibility checklist items (keyboard, screen reader, contrast)
design_decisions: Adopt a single annotation layer with semantic priority slots rather than multiple independent overlays to simplify collision logic
Prioritize persistent validation messages (errors/warnings) over ephemeral hints; ephemeral hints should collapse into a single contextual disclosure control when space is constrained
Use token-driven min-heights to avoid vertical collapse; line-clamp hints to 2 lines in compact mode with explicit 'expand' affordance
Provide a CSS-first solution (tokens + utilities) and a small JS module to manage disclosure and aria-live updates for screen readers
Animations for annotation entrance should be suppressed when 'prefers-reduced-motion' or when CPU-constrained telemetry indicates a high load

comments: 2026-03-02 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after UX review of support incidents. Initial research plan attached. Blocking: need engineering bandwidth for spike.

2026-03-04 Priya Gomez: Completed initial audit of 12 customer forms. Found three dominant collision patterns: (1) trailing helper + error, (2) inline suggestion list pushing adjacent control, (3) multi-column labels that reflow over hints. Uploaded samples to Figma.
2026-03-06 Marco Liu: Drafted token proposal (spacing-slim-01..03, annotation-z-01, field-min-h-compact). Will convert to tokens.json and share in Monday's sync.
2026-03-08 Sam Ortega: Started Storybook spike. CSS-first approach seems feasible; small JS needed to manage aria-live updates and collapse toggles. Early perf numbers look good.

2026-03-10 Lina Okoye: Accessibility review: error messages must be surfaced to screen readers immediately via aria-live='assertive' for errors only; hints should use polite. Need to confirm desired behavior for warning state. Recommend including keyboard expand/collapse affordance for collapsed hints.
